title: Napoleon's strategy at Ulm
subject: histoire
description: In October 1805, Napoleon surrounded and captured **60,000 Austrians** in two weeks, almost without a major battle. Ulm shows the power of speed.

hero.hook: In two weeks, Napoleon captured an entire army... without fighting the great battle.

blocks.text: In October **1805**, **Napoleon Bonaparte**, emperor of the French for less than a year, achieved a rare feat. In two weeks, he surrounded and captured an Austrian army of approximately **60,000 men**, almost without a major pitched battle.
The campaign is set around **Ulm**, a fortified city in southern Germany on the Danube. Napoleon proves that you can win by speed and secrecy, not just by head-on collision.

England finances an alliance against France: the **Third Coalition**. It brings together the Austria of Emperor **Francis II** and Russia of Tsar **Alexander I**. But Austria is not waiting for the Russians. General **Karl Mack**, who commands the Austrian army, pushes around **70,000 people** to Ulm. He believes the place is impregnable.

blocks.caption: Napoleon Bonaparte, Emperor for less than a year in 1805.

blocks.text: The Russian army used the Julian calendar, offset by **12 days** compared to the Austrians. This confusion further delayed the arrival of reinforcements and isolated Mack at Ulm.

Mack awaits the French from the west, from the [[Black Forest]], a massif in southwest Germany. He neglects his sides and his rear. Meanwhile, the Russians under General **Kutuzov** are still far to the east.

Napoleon briefly abandoned the idea of ​​invading England. He pivots his [[Grande Armée]] towards Germany. Its asset: the [[The Napoleonic Army Corps]]. Each corps is a small autonomous army, with its infantry, cavalry and cannons. Seven bodies walk on parallel roads.

On **September 25**, approximately **210,000 men** crossed the Rhine. Marshal **Murat**, Napoleon's brother-in-law and leader of the cavalry, directs Mack's attention to the west. Meanwhile, other marshals (Bernadotte, Davout, Soult, Ney, Lannes) bypassed Ulm from the north, at nearly **30 km per day**.
On **October 7**, the French crossed the Danube behind Mack. It is cut off from Vienna, the Austrian capital, and the Russians. The Ulm trap has closed.

sections.title: An army that surrenders without a big battle

blocks.text: Mack tries to get out, notably to **Elchingen**, a neighboring village. Marshal **Ney** seizes the heights. On **October 17, 1805**, Mack surrenders: **27,000** soldiers lay down their arms on the spot. In total, Austria lost approximately **60,000 men** in the campaign.

blocks.caption: The surrender of Ulm: an army captured almost without a decisive battle.

blocks.text: After the capitulation, Napoleon invited the Austrian officers to dinner. Mack introduced himself as follows: “Here is the unfortunate Mack. » The Emperor returned his sword to him.

It is a victory of the legs as much as of courage. But the same week, at [[The Battle of Trafalgar (October 21, 1805)]], off the coast of Spain, British Admiral Nelson destroyed the Franco-Spanish fleet. Napoleon reigns on the continent. England keeps the sea.

The road to **Vienna** opens. The French entered on **November 13**. Then, on December 2, 1805, at **Austerlitz** (in present-day Czechia), Napoleon defeated the Austrians and Russians. Ulm becomes a model: paralyze the enemy before hitting him. In an attempt to ruin England in another way, Napoleon soon invented [[Continental blockade]], which banned European trade with London.

blocks.text: In October **1805**, Napoleon captured **60 000** Austrians at Ulm almost without a decisive battle: speed and maneuver were as valuable as frontal shock.
